events.title: THE WINTER STORES ARE REBALANCED FOR THE FINAL COLD WEEKS
events.body: The estate stewards conduct a second winter accounting after comparing the January consumption figures with the stores held at the principal and outlying properties. The figures show that the reserve remains usable, but fodder and firewood require tighter distribution if the remaining cold weeks are to be covered without an emergency purchase. Valerius orders the stewards to consolidate the most vulnerable stores and to keep a written record of every transfer between the holdings. Granary keepers begin moving small quantities before shortages can develop at individual locations. The work does not create a new supply system, but it makes the existing one more deliberate and centralized. The revised schedule becomes the basis for the estate's preparations for the approach of spring.

events.title: THE RAID DOSSIER RECEIVES ITS REQUESTED CLARIFICATIONS
events.body: The clarification sent from Valerius's records reaches the correspondence associated with Quintus Caecilius Metellus Celer. The reply confirms receipt of the chronology and asks that copies of two supporting statements be retained with the original account rather than circulated separately. Valerius has his scribes compare the copies against the estate's existing notes before sending the requested material onward. Aulus Vettius remains involved as an intermediary in the documentary chain, while no new accusation is attached to his name. The exchange makes the inquiry more documentary in character and gives Valerius a clearer record of what has actually been submitted. The dossier consequently moves forward without requiring a new public confrontation.

events.title: LAKE-PORT MERCHANTS RESERVE SPACE FOR THE FIRST SPRING CARGOES
events.body: The merchants who had been arranging the next lake-port cycle now begin reserving actual warehouse space for cargoes expected when transport conditions improve. Their agreements remain preliminary, but the reservations show that the commercial preparations have moved beyond simple discussion. Estate administrators compare the commitments with the storage capacity already recorded during the winter inspections. Warehouse workers clear several occupied sections and repair packing platforms that had been left unused during the coldest part of the season. No extraordinary profit is realized yet, and no new harbor construction is undertaken. The estate's existing commercial network is beginning to turn from winter preparation toward active spring traffic.

events.title: THE BOUNDARY PETITION BRINGS NEIGHBORING SMALLHOLDERS TOGETHER
events.body: The boundary petition first raised during the January readings develops into a joint appearance by several neighboring smallholders. Rather than arriving as separate complainants, the farmers bring a common description of the disputed access route and identify the points at which their field records differ. Valerius receives the statements and orders that the relevant boundaries, paths, and older written descriptions be compared before any decision is made. The gathering remains orderly, and neither the petitioners nor the opposing interests receive a ruling during the meeting. The estate scribes begin assembling a single packet so that the dispute can be examined without relying on competing oral recollections alone. The episode gives the library's local reading circle an unexpectedly practical connection to the administration of neighboring land.

events.title: MARCELLUS'S QUESTIONS RETURN TO THE ESTATE IN A NEW LETTER
events.body: A new letter associated with Marcus Claudius Marcellus returns to the estate with questions arising from the material sent during the January readings. The questions concern passages and arguments discussed by the local readers, and the letter asks Valerius to preserve the differences between the local explanations rather than reduce them to a single summary. Valerius's scribes copy the letter and prepare a response using the notes already gathered at the estate. The exchange remains intellectual and personal, without creating a formal political office or appointment. Several readers are invited to add their own observations before the reply is sealed. The correspondence continues to widen the circle around the estate library while preserving the local character of the discussions.

events.title: THE FIRST SPRING PREPARATIONS BEGIN ON THE MOST EXPOSED FIELDS
events.body: As the weather begins to permit limited work, estate workers start preparing the fields identified during the January assessment. The first crews concentrate on the sections that require the most clearing and repair before ordinary planting work can begin. Stewards record the work separately from the winter stores so that labor and material requirements for the coming agricultural cycle can be compared with the previous season. Nearby smallholders are also seen beginning their own preparations, giving the estate administrators a clearer sense of the timing of local field activity. No change in land ownership occurs, and the existing holdings remain unchanged. The first practical work of the agricultural year nevertheless marks the transition from winter preservation toward production.

events.title: THE ESTATE'S WINTER ACCOUNTS ARE CLOSED AHEAD OF THE SPRING CYCLE
events.body: At the end of February the stewards close the winter administrative accounts and place the storage, field, correspondence, and maintenance records together for Valerius's review. The combined packet shows that the estate has passed through the winter without a major disruption, although the stores have required increasingly careful allocation. The agricultural notes now sit beside the commercial commitments and the unresolved local petition, giving the next season a more complicated administrative agenda than the previous one. Valerius instructs the scribes to preserve the full packet rather than discard intermediate working notes. The decision keeps the documentary trail intact for the estate's own administration and for the correspondence already developing with Roman contacts. February therefore ends with several separate threads still active and ready to produce consequences as the spring cycle advances.
